entries.finding_non_trade_cash_credit: CASH MOVED WITHOUT A TRADE, AND THE RECONCILIATION IS WHAT CAUGHT IT. Every prior post-close run of this trading day (23:19Z, 00:19Z, 01:18Z, 02:19Z) recorded cash at exactly $1,046.96; this run reads $1,052.10, +$5.14. RULED OUT BY BROKER READ, not by inference: get_realized_pnl(2026-08-31..2026-08-31) returns number_of_trades 0 / total_returns 0, and get_equity_orders(created_at_gte=2026-08-31) returns exactly ONE order all day -- the 13:37:54Z MMM buy, 2.884552 sh @ 173.3371, placed_agent agentic -- so no sale, no partial, no unauthorized fill. All five equity quantities and the single option quantity are byte-identical to the 02:19Z read, so it is not a position change. pending_deposits is 0, so it is not a transfer. MOST LIKELY CAUSE, stated as a hypothesis and NOT as a confirmed fact: a month-end cash-sweep interest credit. 2026-08-31 is the last business day of August, and ~4-4.5% APR on the ~$1,000-1,550 cash this account carried through the month is ~$4-6, which brackets $5.14. A dividend is the alternative but no single plausible per-share amount on ROST/LLY/PNC/MDLZ/MMM lands at $5.14 on these fractional sizes, and MMM was bought today so cannot have paid one. NO TOOL AVAILABLE TO THIS DESK SETTLES IT -- the connector exposes orders and realized P/L but no cash-transaction ledger, so the next run should NOT expect to confirm it either and must not re-flag it as unexplained drift.
entries.why_it_is_worth_recording_at_all: MATERIALITY IS NIL AND THAT IS THE POINT. $5.14 gates nothing: it moves deployable capital from $849.97 to $855.11 against a 5%-of-total operational reserve of $196.99, changes no cap, no throttle and no sizing decision, and no trade was placeable anyway with the market shut. entries.the_entry_and_why_it_reverses_yesterdays: THIS IS THE DECISION WORTH AUDITING. The 2026-08-31T16:45Z run wrote _A_DECLINE_THROUGH_POSITIVE_NEWS_IS_STRONGER_THAN_A_NEWSLESS_DRIFT about THIS EXACT NAME: GD fell 2.03% on the day it signed a seven-year DoD multiyear procurement framework while partner LMT fell only 0.44%, graded 'case (c) -- the marginal buyer is absent at this price even when handed a reason to show up', and called that veto 'FIRMER, not weaker'. A run that simply bought GD today without engaging that would be overriding a finding it never read. || PROCEDURE ACTUALLY FOLLOWED, per _VETOES_HAVE_DIFFERENT_HALF_LIVES: re-read the original decline, identify which veto was BINDING, and test whether it decayed -- never re-test in isolation and read expiry as a green light. BOTH GD vetoes were tape-class and BOTH inverted. (1) The complex de-rate: 08-31 measured ITA -2.10% = 4.4x SPY, which _COMPLEX_VETOES_NEED_A_MAGNITUDE_TEST confirmed as a genuine de-rate. Today the same measurement gives ITA +0.534% against SPY -0.678%, with ALL SIX primes green -- an advance, not merely an absence of decline. (2) Case (c) is refuted by the cleanest test available: the marginal buyer who was absent on announcement day showed up the very next session, across the whole complex, with the index down 0.7%. || The STRUCTURAL veto never bound: GD is below 2 of 3 averages (SMA20 387.00, SMA50 376.41) but ABOVE SMA130 357.42 by +3.9% and only -6.2% off its highest close in 145 bars, so it never met the _RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC decline rule (below ALL three). entries.finding_iv_day_over_day_needs_a_time_off: A DAY-OVER-DAY ATM-IV DIFF IS ONLY MEANINGFUL IF BOTH READINGS WERE TAKEN AT THE SAME TIME OF DAY, AND MOST ROWS IN iv_history.json DO NOT RECORD WHEN THEY WERE TAKEN. Raw diffs: SPY +3.73%, QQQ +1.20%, NVDA -2.01%, AMD -6.97%, TSM -2.99%, AVGO -0.91%, MSFT -3.08%, TSLA -1.43%. SURVIVING THE CORRECTION: only SPY and QQQ (which ROSE despite an artifact pushing down, so index vol genuinely firmed on a risk-off session and is if anything understated) and AMD (down ~5.5% more than the artifact explains, on a -2.65% session -- vol FALLING into a sharp price drop). The other five carry little or no signal. THE NEAR MISS: six of six single names printed lower and two of two ETFs higher -- a textbook dispersion signature, internally consistent, and exactly the confluence the 2026-08-28 mid-event finding warns reads as conviction when it is one artifact applied uniformly. entries.finding_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE: THE HEADLINE: the mechanical take-profit's two gates -- RSI2>=70 and price>entry -- are NEAR-INDEPENDENT, so both can be true at a gain of a few cents. MEASURED on MDLZ: RSI2 crosses 70 at 62.7337, which is +0.230% from the 62.5899 entry = $1.15 gross on 7.988509 sh, against the position's own written target of 64.70 = $16.86. The clause would bank 6.8% of the trade's stated objective and consume a book slot doing it. || MECHANISM (the transferable part): RSI2 is a function of the recent PRICE PATH, P/L a function of the ENTRY LEVEL. The price at which the authority fires is set by one thing, the size of what it banks by another. A position entered at or near a local high -- exactly what a mean-reversion entry filled in the opening window tends to be, per the 13:52Z opening-window slippage finding -- satisfies both gates at a trivial gain. The worse the entry, the smaller the gain at which the exit fires: the clause pays least where execution was worst. || THIS IS THE MIRROR OF THE HOLE ALREADY FIXED, IN THE SAME SENTENCE. The 2026-08-26 correction added price>entry to stop the exit realizing a LOSS on a technical bounce (it fired on PNC at RSI2 78.5 while 0.34% underwater). That fix is right and stands -- but it bounds only the SIGN of the outcome, never its MAGNITUDE, and nobody checked the other end. This file's most-repeated shape: a rule written against one failure mode assumed to have bounded the whole quantity. || THE RULE: an RSI2>=70 print is a mechanical take-profit only when the gain is worth banking against the trade's OWN written target -- roughly a third of the entry-to-target distance as a working floor. Below that it is an OPTIONAL exit-into-strength needing a HARD RULE 7 thesis break or a graded rotation reason, never a technical trigger alone. Identical resolution to the 2026-08-26 underwater case, applied to the trivially-green one. No other gate changes. || HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, because it is not one-sided: selling MDLZ at 62.73 frees ~$501 and takes deployable from $302.10 to ~$803, which is the difference between a book that can enter and one that cannot. That is real. But it is a ROTATION argument, and rotation requires a GRADED incoming idea that beats the position sold. None exists this run. Freeing capital for an idea you have not had yet is selling on the hope of a signal. || HONEST SCOPE: it changed no decision -- MDLZ printed 66.07, not 70, so the authority was never armed. That is the only condition under which a filter's own thresholds can be audited credibly, the same standard the volume-baseline findings hold themselves to. n=1 name; the one-third fraction is a judgement, not a measured optimum. What is established firmly is the STRUCTURAL point: no bound on the gain follows from either gate. || DETECTOR, two lines of arithmetic off numbers already in the ledger: compute the gain at the trigger price and the gain at the written target. If the first is a small fraction of the second, the clause fired on its technical leg with its economic leg absent -- decline and say which.

finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.claim: THE COHORT RULE'S EXCEPTION CLAUSE -- 'the single green name is the one worth working' -- IS BIASED TOWARD SELECTING EX-DIVIDEND NAMES, AND NEEDS A DIVIDEND CHECK AND A SECTOR-RELATIVE CHECK BEFORE IT FIRES. Both are free from calls the run already makes.
finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.measured: GS read +0.622% against adjusted_previous_close 1020.90 -- which sits EXACTLY $5.00 below the raw previous_close 1025.90, i.e. GS went ex-dividend today. Against the raw close it is +0.132%, essentially flat. And XLF was +0.399% at the same timestamp, so on either measure GS LAGS its own sector rather than leading the cohort. The exception is an artifact twice over. LMT shows the same mechanic in the other direction: adjusted 557.78 vs raw 561.23 ($3.45, also ex-dividend), reading -0.489% adjusted against -1.101% raw. Two of twenty names carried an adjustment, so it is not a rare edge case.
finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.mechanism: A dividend adjustment shifts the denominator of the day-change calculation without any trade occurring, crediting the name with the dividend it just paid away. On a day when the whole cohort is red, an ex-dividend name is therefore the MOST LIKELY name to appear green -- precisely the name where greenness is least informative about whether buyers are present.
finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.detector: When the cohort yields exactly one green name, before working it: (a) compare adjusted_previous_close to previous_close on that name -- any gap is a corporate action, and the RAW figure is the one that says whether it actually traded up; (b) quote its sector ETF at the same timestamp and require the name to BEAT it, not merely to be green while the sector is green.
finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION. The entry was declined on the cohort distribution before the exception was examined, and would have been declined had GS been genuinely green -- one session of relative strength does not repair a weak setup, as the parent finding already states. Recorded because a filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not license a trade. n=1 green name on n=1 session: the MECHANISM is general, the magnitude is not.
finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.family: Same class as the affordability-tier bug (spot price / ATM strike / wrong expiry board), the four denominator modes, and the entry-day-bar error -- a number taken from a convenient field that was never quite the thing being asked about. First appearance in the EQUITY cohort screen rather than an options or volume input.

finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.headline: THE 2026-08-28 DIRECTION RULE IS CORRECT AND ITS PRESCRIBED SUBSTITUTION IS AN UNDERESTIMATE -- BECAUSE THE ONE DEFECTIVE MINUTE THAT CORRUPTS THE BUCKET IS ITSELF A TERM IN THE 1-MINUTE SUM YOU SUBSTITUTE. Measured 9.5-11%, in the dangerous direction.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.how_this_run_came_to_measure_it: The 15:00Z run flagged a 14:40Z hole on both indices, deliberately did NOT correct it (no volume baseline was load-bearing that run), and handed the reconciliation to whichever run first used the bucket. This run makes session-extreme claims that depend on it, so the debt was owed here. That handoff protocol worked exactly as designed and is worth keeping.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.reconciliation_performed: SPY 14:40Z bucket reported 2,280 against a 1-minute sum of 127,793 = -98.2%; QQQ reported 4,436 against 96,260 = -95.4%. Both are materially BELOW their sums, so per the 2026-08-28 direction rule the BUCKET is the holed side and the sum substitutes. Both reported volumes equal their 14:44 one-minute bar EXACTLY (2,280 and 4,436) -- the documented single-constituent signature -- and SPY's bucket OHLC is byte-for-byte its 14:44 minute (764.050/764.105/764.105/764.025). CONTROL in the same call: IWM's 14:40Z bucket reported 128,392 against a 128,336 sum = +0.04%, CLEAN.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.the_new_part: The 14:44 one-minute bar is ITSELF holed by this file's own recognition test -- a bar that is a tiny fraction of BOTH neighbours. SPY 14:44 = 2,280 = 12.9% of the prior minute (17,717) and 12.3% of the next (18,509); QQQ 14:44 = 4,436 = 30.8% / 30.0%. So the substituted 1-minute sum still carries the defective minute as one of its five terms. Imputing 14:44 at its neighbour mean gives a true bucket of ~143,626 (SPY) and ~106,422 (QQQ), against substituted floors of 127,793 and 96,260 -- the prescribed fix UNDERSTATES by 11.0% and 9.5%.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.why_it_matters_and_the_direction: It understates a VOLUME DENOMINATOR, which is the confirmation-manufacturing direction this file has now recorded four separate ways (session-average too strict, trailing-local too easy in a decaying tape, closing-auction too easy in absolute terms, holed-bucket too low). A trailing baseline built on the substituted sum is still ~10% light, so a candidate bar clears it ~10% too easily. The correction does not repair that; it BOUNDS it.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: The 5-minute bucket did not merely under-report -- it ADOPTED the defective minute wholesale, OHLC included. So the bad minute and the bad bucket are ONE defect observed at two resolutions, not two independent ones. That is why the direction rule works at all, and equally why its substitution cannot be exact: you are summing a series that contains the very corruption you are correcting for.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.the_rule_to_apply: Treat a direction-rule substitution as a FLOOR, and label it one. When the bucket's reported volume EXACTLY equals one constituent minute, check that minute against its own neighbours before summing; if it also carries the hole signature, impute it at the neighbour mean and state the result as a range (floor = raw sum, estimate = sum with the bad minute imputed). On a borderline confirmation call, use the imputed figure -- it is the conservative one, because a larger denominator makes confirmation harder.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.honest_scope: THIS CHANGED NO DECISION, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. No trigger was tested this run and no volume baseline was load-bearing. Both session-extreme claims survive the correction with room: SPY's true 14:40Z bucket high is 764.340, below the 764.549 session high set by the 14:35 bar; QQQ's is 710.2297, below the 711.090 set at 14:48. The imputation is an ESTIMATE from two neighbouring minutes, not a measurement -- the 9.5-11% figure is indicative, and n=2 symbols on one bucket. IWM's cleanliness in the identical window is read in ONE direction only, per the 2026-08-27 caveat: cross-symbol agreement evidences a hole, a clean third symbol evidences nothing.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.and_the_offset_hypothesis_stays_dead: Today's holes land at :40, against 08-28's :05/:05/:20 and 08-27's :45. The 2026-08-28 conclusion that hole offsets carry NO information is re-confirmed. Reconcile every window you intend to use; never skip on a positional prior.

finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.summary: The 14:35Z run measured an oversold cohort at 20 names, mean -1.97% vs SPY -0.40%, 1 of 20 green -- and found that single green name was an ex-dividend artifact AND lagging its own sector, concluding the cohort rule's exception clause needs TWO FREE CHECKS before it fires: (1) is the green a name-specific artifact, and (2) is the name leading or lagging its sector. This run applied that clause to a fresh case and it produced the OPPOSITE verdict. That is the useful result: a filter that has only ever vetoed is indistinguishable from a filter that always vetoes.
finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.the_case: LLY is the only one of the book's six equities green on the day: 1172.2782 against a 1156.73 prior close = +1.344%, while SPY is -0.475% and QQQ -0.985%. finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.check_one_name_specific_artifact: FAILS TO DISQUALIFY. finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.check_two_leading_or_lagging_its_sector: FIRES AFFIRMATIVELY, and this is the check that settles it. Measured 15:24Z against prior closes: XLV +0.706% | ABBV +1.542% | LLY +1.344% | MRK +1.171% | JNJ +0.948% | AMGN +0.854% | PFE +0.615% | NVO +0.607% | BMY +0.389%. finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.verdict: NOT AN ARTIFACT. LLY's outperformance is genuine sector participation. The correct characterisation of the tape is therefore a DEFENSIVE ROTATION -- money into health care, out of the Nasdaq (-0.985%), with financials giving back the morning firmness four earlier runs carried (XLF +0.399% at 14:26Z, now -0.268%). finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.transferable_lesson: AN EXCEPTION CLAUSE THAT HAS ONLY EVER VETOED HAS NOT BEEN TESTED -- it has been ASSUMED. The 14:35Z clause was written from one case where both checks disqualified the green name, and a clause validated only by its own confirming instance is the same defect this file has now recorded repeatedly in the volume-baseline arc: a filter that rejects everything looks like discipline and looks like a bug from the same distance. The first case that makes it FIRE is worth more than the case that created it, because it is the only evidence the clause discriminates rather than merely refuses. Apply the same standard to the next filter written from a single instance.
finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. LLY is underwater -1.47% against its 1189.7553 entry, so the profit-banking gate (price > entry) fails and no exit is available whatever the green means; and the equity book is capital-bound at $302.10 deployable, so no entry could act on a defensive-rotation read either. n=1 in the confirming direction does not make the clause reliable -- it makes it non-vacuous, which is a strictly weaker and still worth-having claim.

entries.union_merge_bug_caught: MEASURED WHILE PERFORMING THIS UNION, and it is a defect in HOW a union is done rather than in any run's trading: a first attempt de-duplicated on the key (run_utc, headline[:80]) and produced 812 entries where the correct union is 816. FOUR distinct historical entries -- 2026-08-13T18:30Z, 2026-08-13T23:29Z, 2026-08-14T17:15Z, 2026-08-14T19:15Z -- predate the `headline` field, so their key collapsed to (timestamp, empty string) and the second of each pair was silently dropped. The union protocol says keep BOTH entries; a dedup key built from a field that is not universal quietly violates it. THE RULE: when unioning trade_journal.json, de-duplicate on EXACT serialized content (json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True)) and NEVER on a composite of chosen fields, then ASSERT the expected count (len(shared) + one entry per colliding run) before writing. Same shape as the git diff --stat rule and the lot-invariant assertion: trust the check, not your reading of the merge.

rost_exit_decision.signal: The 15:01Z intraday report grades ROST 'SELL / TAKE-PROFIT -- RSI2 70.6 overbought, swing bounce done'. Both mechanical gates are genuinely satisfied: RSI2 >= 70 AND price > entry (230.73 vs 230.1512, +0.25%). This is the first time the mechanical take-profit authority has actually fired on a green ledger position.
rost_exit_decision.overlay_check_performed_first: Per _REPORT_RSI2_ON_HELD_NAMES_IS_A_LIVE_OVERLAY the report's number was re-derived before it decided anything. Broker settled RSI2 through 2026-09-01 = 35.547. Wilder RSI2 recomputed on the 27 settled closes with the live 230.73 appended = 71.91, reproducing the report's 70.6 at its own 230.62 price. The report is CORRECT and the flag is genuinely firing -- the overlay check confirmed the signal rather than dissolving it, which is the opposite of the LLY case at 14:22Z.
rost_exit_decision.why_declined: MAGNITUDE FLOOR, per _MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR. Entry 230.1512, target 244.66, so the objective is 14.5088/sh = $29.02 on 2 shares. The rule requires the banked gain to be at least ~a third of the entry-to-target distance, i.e. price >= 234.9875. Solved by bisection, ROST's RSI2 crosses 70 at 230.5621 -- $4.43 BELOW that floor, banking $0.82 gross = 2.83% of the objective. At the live 230.73 it is $1.16 gross, 3.99% of the objective, and $0.64 net at the 230.47 bid after the 0.11% spread. Below the floor the print is an OPTIONAL exit-into-strength needing a HARD RULE 7 thesis break or a graded rotation reason -- never a technical trigger alone.
rost_exit_decision.rotation_leg_also_declined: Selling ROST would free ~$460 and unblock the day's deferred UNP entry, so the rotation was tested rather than assumed. It fails on reward: UNP's target is ~299.74 against a live 290.88 = +3.0% remaining, versus ROST's 244.66 against 230.73 = +6.0% remaining. Rotating a 6.0% remaining objective into a 3.0% one, paying two spreads to bank $0.64, is value-destructive. The 14:22Z run's other two grounds also stand unchanged -- the settled-RSI2 ordering across candidates is a 0.4-point spread at the floor of the indicator and is noise, and no HARD RULE 7 verdict for UNP has ever been performed (that run explicitly declined to claim one).
rost_exit_decision.verdict: HOLD ROST. No sell, no rotation, no entry. The setup has discharged and the position is held on its target, not on its oscillator.

entries.finding: _EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TARGET_THAN_OVERSOLD written to holdings.json. The 17:15Z rotation decline recorded its own honest weakness -- that comparing ROST's REMAINING upside to a candidate's TOTAL upside treats two unequal probabilities as equal, because RSI2 83.2 is extended. Measured on ROST's own 752 daily bars (2023-09-01..2026-09-01), Wilder RSI2 validated by reproducing the desk's independently-measured 35.547 settled reading to three decimals: over 15 sessions the EXTENDED (RSI2>=80) cohort reaches +5.19% intrabar 38.0% of the time against the OVERSOLD (RSI2<10) cohort's 39.8%, with the extended cohort carrying the higher mean (+1.20% vs +0.92%), median (+1.85% vs -0.02%) and positive rate (60.6% vs 49.4%). The asserted asymmetry is not visible in this name's data, so it cannot carry the rotation either way -- and the 17:15Z decline was, if anything, conservative. Second and less comfortable result: the OVERSOLD cohort's median 15-session return is -0.02%, i.e. the entry trigger's edge on this name is a RIGHT-TAIL edge rather than a central-tendency one, which independently supports the magnitude floor from a direction its own derivation never used. Honest scope stated in the key: one name, in-sample on the position being decided, heavily overlapping observations, no significance claimed.

entries.findings: TWO durable keys written to holdings.json. (1) _A_SECTOR_DE_RATE_HIDES_INSIDE_A_NEWSLESS_SINGLE_NAME -- this file's rule ranks a newsless decline as the WEAKER veto, and at the single-name level UNP qualifies; that reading is wrong when the peers moved with it. ALWAYS QUOTE THE PEERS BEFORE CALLING A DECLINE NEWSLESS: one name wandering without a cause is probably noise, three correlated names moving 4.5-5.5% on 1.2-2.4x volume is a cause not yet identified, and the single-name feed is exactly where a sector de-rate is invisible. (2) _SETTLE_MECHANICAL_EXITS_BEFORE_COMPUTING_THE_CAPITAL_GATE -- the rotation gate was disposing of the whole screen on the premise that funding requires a rotation sell, while ROST held a live authorized mechanical exit that would supply funding with none. Correct sequence: settle authorized mechanical exits on their own merits FIRST, then compute the capital gate on the resulting cash, then apply the rotation gate only if deployable is still short. Grading a screen against a capital number an unexercised exit authority can change is a stale denominator. Tested in the correct order today and it changed nothing -- which is the only condition under which a process audit is credible -- but it would flip the answer on a day with an A-grade name.

entries.the_transferable_lesson: AN INTRA-SESSION OUTCOME MEASUREMENT TAKEN AT A LOCAL EXTREME IS A MARK, NOT EVIDENCE. The 232.45 reading sat at the 93.5th percentile of the session's 228.010-232.760 range (an upper bound -- a feed hole can only understate the high, which lowers the percentile); 230.69 sits at 56.4%. The prior run was scrupulous about SCOPE ('n=1... OUTCOME evidence against a desk standard that judges PROCESS') and was still wrong about the NUMBER, because a scope caveat does not protect a quantity sampled at a percentile nobody computed. Sibling of _OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_EQUITY_ENTRIES (four entries at a mean 73.6th percentile): there a bad percentile priced an ENTRY, here it prices an EVIDENCE CLAIM. Detector: before citing an intra-session P/L for or against a policy, compute where that mark sits in the session's own range; above ~the 85th percentile it is a peak, and a peak is not a result.

entries.finding: _TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_EXIT_NEEDS_A_LIVE_ONE (new, in holdings.json). Named here, not re-argued. Two halves: (a) report.py's TIME STOP branch reads only sleeve, entry_date and today -- no price, no rsi2, no ma200 -- so it is pure ledger arithmetic and a stale report cannot gate it; it is also the book's only mechanical loss discipline and prompt v10 never throttles a mechanical exit. (b) the RSI2>=70 branch DOES read a live technical, and the connector's RSI2 is not interchangeable with the report's: measured on the same 2026-09-02 close, MMM 1.1 vs 0.8236 and GD 1.9 vs 1.9442 (agree to <0.3) but ROST 83.2 vs 73.1276 (10.07 apart). The agreement is good at the oversold extreme because a 2-period RSI pinned by two down closes collapses to ~0 under any smoothing, and poor in the upper range where up and down closes mix -- so the ENTRY screen sits where the sources agree and the EXIT trigger sits where they do not.

entries.NEW_DURABLE_FINDING: _THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_THE_SKEW_SLOPE_IS_BIGGER_THAN_THE_OPENING_ARTIFACT (holdings.json). Named here, argued there. One-line version: the IV method logs the ATM strike, the ATM strike moves with spot, and the skew slope is +4.05% (SPY) / +3.49% (QQQ) of relative IV per 1% down-move -- so a day-over-day atm_iv diff on any real-move session is dominated by sliding along the skew, not by the surface. A parity result makes the fix cheap: the fixed-strike call/put average is parity-invariant (SPY's legs rotated exactly -0.000447 / +0.000447 and the average held to six decimals), so re-quoting yesterday's strike on today's board is an exact, one-call correction.

A remote session clones ONCE at container start; on a repo committing every ~15 minutes, clone-time content is hours-to-days behind master, so writing back a file read at run start REPLACES master's version with a stale one and git raises nothing. why_this_exit.what_fired: The 18:03Z committed report fired EXIT-INTO-STRENGTH (underwater — optional) on MDLZ at RSI2 75.5, price 61.99, with the annotation '2d to the time stop (held 12d) — this bounce is likely the better exit price'. Live at decision time: 62.08, +0.73% on a day SPY was -0.44% and every other book name was red. That is the highest price and the highest RSI2 of the entire 12-day hold.
why_this_exit.what_this_is_NOT: NOT the mechanical RSI2>=70 take-profit. That authority is PROFIT-BANKING, gated on price > entry (the 2026-08-26 correction), and MDLZ was underwater, so it was structurally unavailable and was never invoked. NOT a thesis sell either: every invalidation level in the entry plan is intact — no cut to the FY26 guidance, the analyst complex still sits above spot, price is 5%+ above a rising 200-day. Filing it as either would misrepresent the decision.
why_this_exit.the_actual_argument: The time stop fires 2026-09-11 (entry 08-28 + SWING_TIME_STOP_DAYS 14) and is NOT discretionary — it sells green or red. So the only live question was PRICE, never WHETHER. Two facts decide it. (1) The 2026-09-02 amendment written into both HARD RULE 5 and prompt v10 addresses exactly this state: within TIME_STOP_WARN_DAYS (3), 'a position about to be recycled anyway is better sold INTO a bounce than out of one.' Day 12 of 14 is inside that window. (2) 2026-09-11 is the CPI print date (08:30 ET, headline seen 3.4% / core 2.4%), so the mechanical sale would have executed into a macro-conditioned tape — an unknown price two days out versus a known one in hand at the bounce's high.
why_this_exit.the_signal_agrees_with_itself: RSI2 75.5 is the desk's OWN exit level. The book's whole doctrine says an RSI2>=70 print is where a mean-reversion swing is sold; the only reason it is not automatic here is the underwater gate on loss-realization. Forward expectancy from an RSI2 75 print on a mean-reverting name is flat-to-negative by construction, which is why that level is the exit and not an entry.
why_this_exit.steelman_for_holding_and_why_it_loses: MDLZ needed only +0.79% to reach breakeven and was moving that way, so two more sessions might have converted this into a proper green take-profit. Rejected on two grounds: it asks the position to do in 2 sessions what it has not done in 12, through a CPI print; and the green-take-profit scenario needs a CONJUNCTION — price up AND RSI2 still >=70 — while RSI2 at 75.5 mean-reverts down fast. A conjunction is not the base case.
why_this_exit.deviation_duty: Prompt v10 requires quoting the prior instance's written exit plan and arguing against it explicitly. Quoted: 'EXIT PLAN: bank on target 64.70 or an RSI2>=70 print while GREEN (an RSI2>=70 print while UNDERWATER is an optional exit-into-strength, never mandatory).' The plan is right that this is never mandatory, and it was not treated as mandatory. What a day-0 plan cannot price is that the optionality expires: holding on an intact thesis buys the thesis runway only while runway exists, and the time stop removes it. Four earlier runs today (14:12Z, 15:20Z, 15:35Z, 16:45Z) held the same signal correctly, and each gave the SAME stated reason — the bounce was WEAKER than when the plan was written (61.755 / 61.610 vs 61.855 at plan time). That reason is now inverted at 62.08, which is the new fact this run acted on rather than a re-litigation of theirs.

COMPLETES A TAXONOMY: a clean review proves little (08-24), a raised review alert is true (08-24 collateral, 09-10 share count), and now -- a raised error at PLACE time can be FALSE. entries.how_the_two_09-10_collision_findings_fit: The sibling's _THE_REVIEW_GATE_CAUGHT_A_SIBLING_COLLISION governs the moment BEFORE an order: review immediately before placing and treat a raised alert as authoritative, because a broker precheck has its own 1.4-second blind window. grades_considered.SBUX: DECLINE, grade B -- thesis WEAKENED, and it is the only one of the three that got a full HARD RULE 7 workup because it is the only one whose technicals earned it. Technicals are genuinely good: RSI2 1.2 (most oversold non-held name on the board), 200-day SMA rising MONOTONICALLY every one of 22 sessions 95.422 -> 97.818 (+2.51%), price 100.03 = +2.26% above it, which is ~20 SESSIONS of cushion at the SMA's +0.109/session slope (the cushion-in-sessions test, not the percent test). mom12-1 +16.3%. Earnings verified CLEAR: get_earnings_calendar 09-10 +21d returns no SBUX, so nothing inside the 09-24 hold window. WHAT KILLS IT IS THE NEWS: the identifiable driver of the slide is Oppenheimer 2026-09-08, 'Starbucks Valuation Already Reflects Improved Sales' -- perform rating, 'we require a path to greater earnings power to turn bullish at current valuation'. Price was 102.82 in that note and is 100.03 now, i.e. the catalyst is 2 days old and STILL BEING PRICED, not priced out; the trend-maturity gate wants the present tape to confirm a turn and it is confirming continuation (-5.4% vs 20d, -5.0% vs 50d, still making lower prices). Corroborating: an unresolved union boycott called 2026-08-25 by the union representing 12,000+ baristas, open-ended with no contract date; a 08-20 restructuring cutting 104 jobs plus ~120 Nashville-relocation separations; and the fundamentals agreeing with Oppenheimer -- P/E 57.5, P/FCF 31.3, PEG -2.3 (negative = declining earnings), and SBUX is the ONLY name in the report's own oversold-uptrend table carrying no value verdict ('--') while RTX, AMGN, ROST and CL all read 'value'. A mean-reversion swing needs the dip to be a DIP; an analyst de-rating on valuation that the numbers corroborate is a RE-RATING, and HARD RULE 7 says a clean RSI2 print is not a buy when the news says otherwise.
grades_considered.CL: DECLINE, grade C -- on the trend gate, no news workup needed. 200-day rises monotonically (86.389 -> 87.814, +1.65%/22 sessions) but price 87.90 sits +0.10% above it: 0.086 points of cushion against a +0.065/session slope = ~1.3 SESSIONS. That is the KHC condition the 14:20Z run declined at +1.71%, only tighter, and the exact case CLAUDE.md._THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS describes -- being above a barely-rising average is not an uptrend, it is a coin flip on the next two sessions.
grades_considered.ROST: DECLINE, grade B. grades_considered.JNJ: DECLINE, grade B. THESIS IS THE STRONG HALF and it is genuinely intact-to-strengthening: UBS assumed coverage 2026-09-02 with Buy and a $320 PT, calling JNJ 'one of the cleanest stories in large-cap pharma' with no near-term loss-of-exclusivity, seven franchises above $5B each and a $30-40B pipeline opportunity taking growth from a 4-6% to an 8%+ CAGR; HSBC raised its PT to $320 from $290 THIS MORNING (09-10) keeping Buy; FactSet mean PT $281.14 with an overweight consensus (+5.7% over spot); FDA approved IMAAVY for warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia 08-25, the first targeted therapy for it; CE marking for Acuvue Oasys Max granted today; JPMorgan's 09-08 flow work has healthcare ETF outflows reversing with JNJ at 10.72% of XLV; guidance was RAISED in July. EARNINGS CLEAR: JNJ does not appear in get_earnings_calendar(high_market_cap) over 09-10..10-10, and a 14-day hold ends 09-24, so no print inside the window. THE SETUP IS THE WEAK HALF AND IT DECIDES. RSI2 9.7 is the SHALLOWEST oversold print on the 23-name board -- twelve names print deeper. The 200-day SMA is rising monotonically (228.394 -> 236.492 over 22 sessions, +3.55%) but price at 266.07 sits 12.5% ABOVE it: this is a mild orderly drift off a record (278.43 close on 09-03, then -4.4% over five sessions, today only -0.38%), not a stretch with much to revert. A Connors mean-reversion edge scales with the depth of the stretch and there is little here. THE CONSISTENCY TEST IS DECISIVE: AMGN 1.7, MA 3.2, VRTX 3.3, MRK 3.5, TGT 4.0, PFE 4.2 and RTX 4.2 were every one graded and DECLINED on this same board today, and every one is a deeper print than JNJ. Several are the same large-cap-pharma trade with the same sector-rotation tailwind, so JNJ is not categorically better -- it is the same idea with a worse entry. Grading it A while declining seven deeper prints in its own sector would not be selectivity, it would be activity. Per the concentration policy a B gets NO position rather than a small one, and 'fewer must mean more selective, never merely bigger'. VERDICT: good company, weak entry -- no position.

friday_review.equity_exits_by_mechanism: The duty asks how many positions each of the three exits closed. Since SWING_TIME_STOP_DAYS went live 2026-09-02, FOUR swing positions have closed: PNC (time stop, red), ROST (take-profit, green), MDLZ (discretionary exit-into-strength, red, taken 2 sessions from its stop), LLY (time stop, red). So 2 of 4 closed on the time stop outright and a third was driven by the impending one — i.e. THREE OF FOUR closes are attributable to elapsed time rather than to the mean-reversion signal completing. That is exactly the pattern the review is told to watch ('a book where the time stop closes nearly everything is not mean-reverting and the entry trigger needs review'). HONEST SCOPE: n=4 is not evidence of anything and no change is proposed. It is flagged as the specific thing to re-measure once the in-regime sample reaches 20 — which is also the sample that unlocks tuning the time stop at all.
friday_review.drift_check: No preference was overridden this week — but say plainly why, because a clean drift check can reflect discipline or merely inactivity, and here it is mostly the latter. The options sleeve placed nothing since 2026-08-26 (16 days) and the equity book placed nothing since the 09-10 LLY exit. The binding reason is CAPITAL, not restraint: deployable is $14.30 against a ~$600 minimum entry, so under the CAPITAL POLICY every idea must clear the rotation bar (beat the weakest position held) rather than simply be funded. Four positions sit inside the 3-4 target with no thesis broken, so nothing has been rotated. STRUCTURE DRIFT: not assessable — the options book expressed no thesis at all this week, which is the absence of a sample rather than consistency.
friday_review.best_and_worst_decision_judged_on_proces: BEST: the 09-10 LLY time-stop exit. The run recognised that report.py's time-stop branch reads ONLY entry_date and today's date — never RSI2, price, or market data — and therefore that a not-yet-landed report could not change the answer, so the stale-report clause (which exists to block trading off stale MARKET signals) did not gate it. Correct rule-scoping under time pressure, and it went out RED, which is the mechanism's entire purpose. WORST: none this week rises to a process failure. The near-miss was the same slot's sibling collision — two runs raced the same exit and the broker precheck missed it by 1.4 seconds; the review-gate caught it and no double-sell occurred, but the protection was the broker's, not the desk's.

entries.finding: _A_SINGLE_SCRATCH_TRADE_FLIPPED_THE_SIGN_OF_THE_CALIBRATION_KILL_BRANCH_2026-09-11 in holdings.json — named here, argued there. calibrate.edge_stats() divided the win rate by ALL closes while deriving the breakeven from only the DECIDED ones; the options book's single $0 leg (the 08-26 legged SPY vertical's long leg, closed at its entry price) pushed its margin to -0.35 pts, which is the KILL branch, while net (+$90.00) and expectancy (+$5.29/trade) were unchanged. FIXED IN CODE THIS RUN: win_rate now divides by wins+losses and a `scratches` field is surfaced. The error was DIRECTIONAL — a scratch can only ever drag the measured win rate toward risk-off — which is why it reads as prudence rather than as a bug.

entries.what_was_wrong: The 09-10 remedy for the one-second push race added a 5-attempt rebase+push loop. It handles a REJECTED PUSH but not a CONFLICTED REBASE. When the 16:57Z scheduled fire and the 17:00Z dispatch fire both wrote latest_intraday.md, our replayed commit conflicted, and from then on every `git pull` died with 'unmerged files' -- attempts 2-5 were guaranteed no-ops. The loop logs one generic message for every failure mode, which is why the distinct mechanism stayed invisible.
entries.the_fix: stock-report.yml: the loop now detects a conflicted rebase and resolves it in favour of THIS run's freshly generated board (under rebase the replayed commit is the 'theirs' side), then continues; a conflict outside that file aborts so the next attempt starts clean instead of wedged.
entries.verification: Reproduced in a 3-clone scratch repo: the old loop emitted the CI log's exact error text and wedged at 'UU latest_intraday.md'. The new loop resolved on attempt 1 and PUSHED ON ATTEMPT 2, tree clean, newer board landed, sibling commit preserved in history. YAML parses; the extracted step passes `bash -n` with the workflow expression substituted.

entries.finding: _DAY_TRACK_BAR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH (holdings.json) -- named here, argued there. In short: day_track.opening_range() and atr() read the terse bar keys high/low/open/close; get_equity_historicals returns high_price/low_price/open_price/close_price, so all five accessors KeyError on every real bar. _selftest() passed because its fixtures are hand-built with the terse keys -- the test encoded the same assumption as the bug. Fixed with a _bf() accessor taking both spellings, plus a selftest case pinned to five VERBATIM connector bars so the terse-only path can never pass again. Verified end-to-end on real bars post-fix.

durable_findings_written_named_not_re_ar: holdings.json._DAY_TRACK_IN_PAPER_manage_MUST_BE_FED_THE_ADVERSE_EXTREME_SINCE_THE_LAST_PASS_NOT_THE_CURRENT_PRICE_2026-09-16 -- THE BIG ONE. manage() tests the stop against the price it is handed. LIVE is safe because a resting broker stop fires on the intraday low; PAPER has no resting order, so handing it the current quote silently converts a stopped-out loser into an open winner whenever price recovers between runs. The bias runs ONE WAY -- toward deleting losers -- and feeds graduate(), which decides whether this track goes live with real money. Fix is procedural, not a parameter.

entries.a_mistake_this_run_made_and_caught_befor: THE FIRST RESOLUTION OF THIS CONFLICT WAS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE DELETED THE SIBLING'S WORK. This run checked what the 15:15Z run had changed by diffing TOP-LEVEL keys only (found: none new) and then printing _last_entry_evaluation TRUNCATED TO 2,200 CHARACTERS -- and the sibling's USB grade sits past that cut. From a check that could not see the thing it was checking for, this run concluded the sibling had added nothing to the ledger and that its journal entry's pointer to '_last_entry_evaluation.grades.USB' was DANGLING. Both conclusions were false, the second was written into the union note as a finding about the sibling, and a `git checkout --ours` then discarded a genuinely better grade. Caught by diffing the sibling's commit against the base BEFORE pushing, and fully repaired. THE SHAPE IS THIS REPO'S MOST-REPEATED DEFECT, arriving in the conflict-resolution step rather than in a trade: a check that passes for the wrong reason -- here, an ABSENCE reported by an instrument that was truncated below the depth the claim required. It is the same family as the four measurement bugs already on file (spot price, ATM strike, wrong expiry board, modelled estimate vs quote): the reading was real, it just did not cover the claim built on it. DETECTOR, and it costs one line: when resolving a UNION, never characterise the other run's changes from a truncated print or a top-level key diff -- run `git diff <base> <theirs> -- <file>` and read the actual hunks. An absence is only evidence when the instrument could have shown the presence.

IBKR -3.941% against XLF -2.313% and SPY -0.835%: it fell 1.70x its own sector ETF and 4.72x the index on the very day the Fed delivered the hike that is the NII channel's whole thesis, so the risk-appetite / de-rating channel dominated. It is a THESIS-CHECK verdict on a HELD position and licenses NOTHING -- none of the three company-specific invalidations has occurred, and converting a cross-sectional price measurement into a sale would hand the book the discretionary price stop HARD RULE 5 forbids (same guardrail as the 18:30Z _THE_COHORT_VETO_IS_ENTRY_SIDE_ONLY finding). The transferable half: a two-sided thesis about a DATED event owes a verdict from the run after the event even though the verdict changes nothing, and that is exactly why four runs between 18:00Z and 19:20Z skipped it -- an unactionable measurement decays fastest because nothing errors when it is missed. The sizing is the part that held up: 18.3% of the account rather than the 30% cap, named at entry as the event adjustment, so being on the losing side of the fork costs -$16.22 and not -$27.

_THE_RSI2_BOARD_DOUBLED_ON_ONE_MACRO_LEG_SO_THE_SCREEN_IS_MEASURING_THE_INDEX_NOT_THE_NAME_2026-09-16 -- NAMED here, argued there. 9 -> 19 names (3.9% -> 8.3% of a 229-name universe) inside the single hour of the presser; ten arrivals, none a name-specific event. Connors RSI(2) presumes an IDIOSYNCRATIC pullback inside an intact uptrend, so a board that doubles on one macro leg is a breadth reading wearing a stock screen's clothing -- the arithmetic is fine, the object it refers to changed. Concrete cost if ignored: all three held positions fell today, so the book has ZERO dispersion, and a fourth name off this board funded with the last $711.57 would be a fourth expression of the SAME factor dressed as diversification -- the version of concentration that buys the variance and none of the selection. NOT a veto and must never harden into one; it changes the QUESTION asked of each candidate, never the ANSWER. Detector: count the board against the prior report's count before grading anything off it, and re-ask each arrival against its OWN sector ETF.

new_work_bmy.verdict: B-GRADE -> NO POSITION. Under the 2026-09-02 concentration policy a B-grade gets no position rather than a small one, so this is a decline on merit and does not depend on the capital bar. Three reasons, in order of weight: (1) TAPE DIVERGENCE -- BMY is -0.70% while SPY is +1.09% and its OWN sector ETF XLV is +0.40%. A mean-reversion entry wants the name bouncing with or ahead of the tape; a name falling alone on a broadly green day is still distributing, and this is the discriminator _TAPE_CONFIRMATION_AND_THE_RSI2_SCREEN_ARE_IN_TENSION names. (2) It is the WEAKEST oversold reading on its own board (RSI2 8.7 vs LRCX 2.6, CVS 5.2, VZ 7.7, ABNB 7.8), so under _ROTATION_GATE_IS_ANSWERABLE_FROM_THE_SCREENS_OWN_RANKING it does not even beat the position the book ALREADY HOLDS on the same board. (3) Below a rising 50-day by 1.01% -- marginal rather than broken (cf. PNC at -6.78% this morning), so this is the lightest of the three and is not doing the work on its own.

entries.finding: See holdings.json._THE_MIXED_BOOK_GUARD_FALSE_POSITIVED_ON_A_CORRECTLY_SPLIT_BUCKET_AND_SUPPRESSED_A_KILL_2026-09-21 and ._WEEKLY_CALIBRATION_2026-09-21. Summary only, not re-argued here: calibrate.edge_stats() inferred 'blended sample' from the `side` field, which was a valid proxy only while split_books() ALSO split on `side`. The 2026-09-18 fix moved the split to broker membership, so a correctly-split options bucket (17 actively-closed + 1 lapse) began reading mixed_book=True; recommend() then returned 'REFUSED' and returned EARLY, ahead of the n gate, the in-regime gate AND the KILL branch. Fixed by tagging rows in split_books() and keying the guard on that tag, with a `side` fallback for untagged callers. Seven regression tests pass, including that a genuinely blended sample is still refused. The tempting one-line fix -- let KILL bypass the refusal -- was deliberately NOT taken, because it would re-create the 2026-09-18 contamination bug in mirror image.

200day_gate_killed_three.method: sma(200, day) via get_equity_technical_indicators, last 23 settled values, monotonicity counted over 22 transitions, cushion measured in SESSIONS per _A_RISING_200DAY_CAN_BE_A_WINDOW_ARTIFACT against a 10-session hold.
200day_gate_killed_three.CRM: FAIL. 5 down-ticks in 22, net +0.11% over the window -- the average is FLAT, not rising. Secondary objection independent of the gate: the report's own suggested invalidation sits 13.6% below spot, and on a book that places NO price stop a 13.6% thesis-death level is wide dispersion, not a tight mean-reversion trade (same objection that declined AEHR at 18.1% on 09-01).
200day_gate_killed_three.KHC: FAIL. 10 down-ticks in 22 and the average has ROLLED OVER -- 24.0301 on 09-04 falling monotonically to 23.9976 on 09-21. Spot 24.101 is 0.43% above a FALLING 200-day. Confirms the 2026-09-10 decline of the same name on the same leg.
200day_gate_killed_three.PNC: FAIL, and it is the instructive one. Monotonic rising, 0 down-ticks, +2.74% -- the BEST-looking 200-day on the board by the percent test. Cushion 227.42 - 227.2054 = 0.215 pts against a slope of +0.2756/day = 0.78 SESSIONS. The uptrend certification expires inside ONE session of a ten-session hold.

survivors_to_thesis.VZ: DECLINED, grade B+. Setup is the cleanest on the board: RSI2 1.7 (deepest), 200-day monotonic rising 0/22 down-ticks with a 16.6-session cushion, 12-1 momentum +13.8% (09/2025 close 43.95 -> 08/2026 close 50.02), [ERN] verified clear. Thesis INTACT and not broken by the decline -- the driver is MACRO, a bond-proxy de-rating on rates (Fed hiked 09-16 with dots signalling another, 30-year 5.35% / 10-year ~5.0%, highest since 2007), which is exactly what Connors RSI(2) exists to exploit. Company-specific news is POSITIVE: the 09-08 multi-billion Corning deal for 80M+ miles of fiber 2027-2032 supporting 40-50M broadband passings and long-haul AI backbone; dividend held at $0.7075 (5.66% yield) on 09-09; Samsung ISAC 5G trial 09-15; and MoffettNathanson RAISED its PT $49 -> $50 at 07:08 ET THIS MORNING. WHY IT IS NOT AN A: the 'why NOW' is unanswered. The rate driver is not spent -- it is actively worsening (crude >$100, diesel a record $6.06/gal, core CPI +0.3% m/m), and a mean-reversion entry needs the repricing driver exhausted, not accelerating. Consensus is HOLD-dominant, 10 buy / 18 hold / 0 sell, with only +8.0% to a $50.69 mean PT, and this morning's raise kept a NEUTRAL rating. Compare ABNB at entry: +8.4% to target but an OVERWEIGHT average with targets marking monotonically UP across the decline. SpaceX-into-wireless is a live structural overhang. A B-GRADE GETS NO POSITION, NOT A SMALL ONE -- declined on merits, before the rotation gate.
survivors_to_thesis.BAC: DECLINED, grade C. Technically the setup looks strong -- RSI2 7.4, 200-day monotonic rising with a 23.8-session cushion (the most comfortable on the board), 12-1 momentum +20.1%, [ERN] clear, 21 buy / 6 hold / 0 sell. IT FAILS HARD RULE 7 ON A COMPANY-SPECIFIC GUIDANCE CUT. At an industry conference 2026-09-14 CEO Brian Moynihan guided Q3 sales & trading revenue roughly FLAT y/y and investment banking fees to $1.6-1.8B against ~$2.0B consensus, implying a >10% y/y DECLINE; the stock fell 5.14% that session and has fallen a FURTHER 5.4% since (59.47 -> 56.265), so the catalyst is 8 days old and the reaction is still running rather than completed -- the trend-maturity gate's (b) and (c) both fail. THE STALE-CONSENSUS TRAP, flagged explicitly: the +21.7% upside to the $68.45 mean PT is computed from a figure last updated 2026-09-05, which PREDATES the guidance cut entirely; the only post-event revision on the tape is Goldman CUTTING its target $79 -> $76 on 09-16. Citing the mean PT as bullish evidence here would be exactly the stale-input error this repo keeps catching. A clean RSI2 print is not a buy when the news says otherwise.
